claims.statement: After enterprise setup, administrators may customize package ecosystems available to end users. The fragment links ecosystem configuration and enterprise getting-started guides; optional next steps do not demonstrate enabled support, entitlement or approval to change settings.

GitHub Packages GraphQL API is unavailable for registries with granular permissions; registries supporting only repository-scoped permissions are the eligible class referenced by the linked matrix. This constrains GraphQL beyond deletion despite the filename; eligibility is not actual registry identification, sufficient authorization or executed API evidence.

Package pages expose per-version metadata such as publication dates, descriptions, installation/usage guidance, associated assets and download activity. Descriptive metadata and example links are not verified provenance, safe installation, rights clearance or an actual download receipt; the example was not visited or executed.

The resolved package_registry variable directs using the Role dropdown to select a repository's desired default access level to a package. It does not enumerate roles or establish sufficient permissions, an effective grant or universal repository privileges.
The Actions access sidebar step is conditional on GHES. Navigation is not an access receipt and the absent non-GHES branch does not imply no Actions package support.

Adding a repository uses Manage Actions access on FPT/GHEC and the Add repository button/search in the containing flow otherwise. The screenshot caption identifies the button but is not visual inspection or a verified granted permission; no repository was added.
